title: Route Orchestrator: DSL integrity harness and staged validator for region/tier/fallback rules
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: The policy engine currently mixes parsing, validation, and runtime mapping for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. This makes incremental changes risky, tests brittle, and causes silent compat regressions when new rule syntax or model aliasing is added.

Goal: Introduce a standalone DSL integrity harness and staged validator that: 1) verifies schema/typing for routing rules (regions, tiers, variant fallbacks); 2) emits clear migration hints for deprecated constructs; 3) runs lightweight behavioral checks against a simulated runtime mapping layer to catch mismatches early. The harness should be usable in CI, developer laptops, and can produce machine-readable diagnostics for the Console.

Scope: parsing/AST -> schema/semantic validation -> staged runtime compatibility checks. Does NOT include migrating live runtime data or changing default routing behavior in production. The PR will add validation artifacts and a compatibility mode flag (--strict-routing-checks) that can be toggled per environment.
acceptance_criteria: New DSL harness accepts existing routing rule corpus (sampled from prod) with no false positives under non-strict mode
--strict-routing-checks flags on CI and errors for any deprecated constructs or ambiguous region/tier mappings
Diagnostics output is JSON-lines with fields: file, line, rule_id, severity, message, suggestion
Staged runtime check simulates a request matrix (regions x tiers x model_aliases) and reports unreachable fallbacks
Automated tests covering 12 representative rule patterns (regional affinity, probabilistic splits, tier fallthrough, model alias fallback)
updates: 2026-02-10 Maya Patel: Created ticket after spike; prototype parser dump shows inconsistent alias normalization across regions.
2026-02-15 Liam Chen: Spike complete — built a PoC harness that validates AST shape and flags unknown operators. Found 27 rules in prod corpus that rely on implicit alias resolution.
2026-02-20 Design review (Ana Ruiz): requested clearer UX for diagnostics in Console and an opt-in strict mode for Dedicated customers.
2026-02-25 Security review kickoff (Jordan Kim): flagged requirement for KMS-protected audit logs when diag payloads include customer model ids.
2026-03-01 Implementation: added JSON-lines diagnostic emitter; unit tests for schema validator added (coverage: routing-validator: 84%).
2026-03-03 QA: Integration tests against simulated runtime matrix revealed an edge case where probabilistic weights sum to 0. Fix proposed in parser normalization step.
2026-03-05 Liam Chen: Marking core harness feature gated behind feature flag. Preparing RFC for gradual rollout and migration guidance.
migration_steps: Collect current routing rule corpus from prod (sampling window: last 90 days) and run harness in non-strict mode to baseline
Enable strict checks in staging and fix blocker rules reported by the harness (alias normalization, deprecated operators)
Rollout strict mode to canary account subset (5% of traffic) with monitoring on errors and rollback hooks
Schedule dedicated run for enterprise customers with on-prem deployments to provide migration assistance
Post-rollout: run compatibility scanner weekly and feed aggregated diagnostics to Console as a routing health panel
test_plan: Unit: per-operator schema tests + fuzzing for operator arguments
Integration: simulate 5000 request matrix combinations through staged runtime check; assert no unreachable fallback paths
Regression: run harness nightly against historical corpus and block merges if new high-severity diagnostics appear
Load: ensure harness CI job completes within 6 minutes for a 10k-rule corpus by using incremental checks
risks: False positives blocking deploys if strict checks are enabled prematurely
Large legacy rule sets may rely on implicit behavior that must be documented/migrated
Diagnostics leak sensitive model identifiers unless redaction/KMS protections applied
Performance of CI harness could regress developer velocity if not optimized
notes: Decision: we will not attempt automated rule rewriting in v1 — only emit suggestions and migration hints.
Trade-off: keeping non-strict mode by default preserves compatibility but delays detection of subtle runtime mismatches.
Follow-up: create a small Console panel to surface weekly diagnostics for top-10 customers affected.
Owner for rollout coordination: Maya Patel (infra) + Priya Suresh (solutions)
